extracted.intended_audience: writers, cultural critics, and citizens interested in shaping/portraying American democratic character and culture
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and prescriptive criteria for how democracy should shape national character, culture, and literary representation — i.e., how writers and reformers should portray and cultivate typical American personalities grounded in democratic life. Emphasizes balance between mass democracy and individuality, practical culture, physical health, conscience, and women's roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Democracy's preferred citizen type
rubrics_metrics.description: Democracy 'asks for men and women with occupations, well-off, owners of houses and acres, and with cash in the bank--and with some cravings for literature, too.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ideal democratic constituency is the middling property-owner and active worker; civic stability and democratic endurance depend on a population with occupations, property, and some literary inclination. This is both descriptive (who democracy tends to produce) and prescriptive (what social conditions democracy favors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Literature must speak to the people
rubrics_metrics.description: Few writers 'have yet really spoken to this people, created a single image-making work for them, or absorb'd the central spirit and the idiosyncrasies which are theirs.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writers should aim to address the mass, the 'alert, turbulent, good-natured, independent' crowds of cities and country — create image-making works that absorb and express the spirit of the common people rather than catering to imported elite tastes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject foreign/courtly literary models
rubrics_metrics.description: The models of literature 'as we get it from other lands, ultra-marine, have had their birth in courts, and bask'd and grown in castle sunshine' and are 'poisonous to the idea of the pride and dignity of the common people.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid aristocratic, court-originated models (Shakespeare included in this critique as foreign influence) when creating American literature; prefer native, democratic models that reflect the experiences and dignity of common folk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Culture must be practical and mass-applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: Demand 'a programme of culture ... not for a single class alone, or for the parlors or lecture-rooms, but with an eye to practical life, the west, the working-men, the facts of farms and jack-planes and engineers, and of the broad range of the women also of the middle and working strata.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design cultural education and artistic programs for broad, everyday applicability — practical training and examples for working classes and frontier life — rather than elite salon cultivation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include equality of women and robust motherhood in cultural aims
rubrics_metrics.description: The cultural programme should be 'with reference to the perfect equality of women, and of a grand and powerful motherhood.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any plan for national culture must explicitly make space for women's equality and for motherhood as a central, powerful social role — both as social policy and as subjects/themes in literature and culture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve and cultivate individuality (personalism)
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuality is 'the pride and centripetal isolation of a human being in himself' and is the indispensable counterpart to the leveling force of democracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While promoting democratic equality, actively protect and encourage unique personal identity and 'idiocrasy' — art and institutions should nourish distinct selves rather than flattening into conformity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance intellect/culture with native selfhood
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'enlargement of intellect' and stores of knowledge are overweening; the danger is slighting 'the precious idiocrasy and special nativity and intention that he is, the man's self.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Educational and cultural cultivation should not swamp or overwrite native personal character; intellectual training must be balanced by safeguards for originality and individual purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical robustness as cultural ideal
rubrics_metrics.description: The model personality requires 'a clear-blooded, strong-fibred physique' and attentiveness to 'food, drink, air, exercise, assimilation, digestion' producing a healthy presence, flush complexion, erect attitude, powerful voice, and steady gaze.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical health and bodily vigor are foundational for ideal citizens and artists; cultivation programs should include physiologic attention (nutrition, exercise, healthy habits) as essential to character-formation and cultural vitality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Favor 'healthy rudeness' over over-refinement
rubrics_metrics.description: Warning that 'refinement and delicatesse ... threaten to eat us up' and that 'Provision for a little healthy rudeness, savage virtue, justification of what one has in one's self ... is demanded.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid excessive polish and gentility that erode robustness and authenticity — allow for roughness, singleness, and normal simplicity as virtues rather than always smoothing into etiquette and artifice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate an invariable conscience
rubrics_metrics.description: The simple, unsophisticated Conscience is 'probably the least attended to in modern times' but indispensable; without it 'the triumphant modern civilizee ... will still show himself but an amputation.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moral formation — an internally applied sense of right — must be central to individual development; education and culture should inculcate conscience as a non-negotiable trait.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religiousness as individual spiritual depth
rubrics_metrics.description: The ripeness of Religion is to be 'a part of the identified soul' and 'does not depend at all upon' churches; only in 'the perfect uncontamination and solitariness of individuality' may real spirituality emerge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage private, inward spiritual cultivation and awe that arises from individual identity rather than institutionally prescribed religion; art and culture should respect and foster solitary spiritual experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Politics as formative practice; eschew party subservience
rubrics_metrics.description: Political democracy 'supplies a training-school for making first-class men' and 'It is the fashion ... to decry ... the active politics of America,' but Whitman advises 'always inform yourself; always do the best you can; always vote. Disengage yourself from parties.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote active, informed participation in politics as character-building while warning against blind allegiance to parties and partisan dictators; encourage independent, critical civic engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop a systematic science of healthy average personalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggests 'a science as it were of healthy average personalism, the object of which should be to raise up and supply through the States a copious race of superb American men and women, cheerful, religious.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocate for organized, perhaps pedagogical, approaches to nurture robust, typical American personalities at scale — a deliberate program combining physical, moral, and cultural training for the masses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portray diverse, practical female archetypes
rubrics_metrics.description: Whitman presents several female models — the independent seamstress who preserves dignity; the woman running a mechanical business who 'has not lost the charm of the womanly nature'; the wife/mother who makes domestic duties 'illustrious'; the elderly 'Peacemaker' who is socially wise and magnetically neighborly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When representing women, favor practical independence, competence in work and household duties, preserved womanly charm and moral authority — depict varied, real-life female characters rather than imported novelistic courtly types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Produce typic personalities rather than imported types
rubrics_metrics.description: We must 'entirely recast the types of highest personality from what the oriental, feudal, ecclesiastical worlds bequeath us' and instead create 'a typical personality of character, eligible to the uses of the high average of men.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artists and cultural planners should invent and represent native American types that fit democratic conditions — accessible, robust, and broadly applicable models — not transplanted aristocratic or exotic personae.
